hints: Look closely at the structure of 2-bromo-2-methylpropane and notice what type of halogenoalkane it is.
Remember that a tertiary halogenoalkane reacts with aqueous NaOH by SN1, so the first step involves only the C-Br bond breaking with no OH- involved.
Check where the curly arrow starts and ends, it must start on the C-Br bond and finish on the Br to show Br leaving with the electron pair.
walkthrough:
**Identify the substrate**

Look at 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, $(CH_3)_3CBr$. The C attached to Br is attached to three other carbons, so it is a tertiary halogenoalkane.

$$ (CH_3)_3C-Br \text{ with } C^{\delta+} - Br^{\delta-} $$

**Choose the mechanism**

Tertiary halogenoalkanes are bulky, so $OH^-$ cannot attack directly. They react by $S_N1$ in aqueous NaOH to form an alcohol.

$$ (CH_3)_3CBr + OH^- \rightarrow (CH_3)_3COH + Br^- \text{ via } S_N1 $$

**Describe the first step of SN1**

The slow first step is heterolytic fission of the polar C-Br bond alone to form a carbocation and bromide ion. No $OH^-$ takes part yet.

$$ (CH_3)_3C-Br \rightarrow (CH_3)_3C^+ + Br^- $$

**Apply curly arrow rules**

A curly arrow shows a pair of electrons moving. It must start in the middle of the C-Br bond and point to Br, showing Br taking both electrons.

$$ C-Br \text{ bond } \curvearrowright Br $$

**Select the correct diagram**

Only the diagram showing ionisation alone with the correct arrow from bond to Br matches the first step of $S_N1$.

options.A: Incorrect. This shows only the C-Br bond, which is right for SN1, but the curly arrow is drawn in the wrong direction. It does not show the electron pair moving from the bond onto Br.
options.B: Correct. This shows the SN1 ionisation step alone with no OH- involved. The curly arrow starts on the C-Br bond and points to Br, correctly showing heterolytic fission to give $(CH_3)_3C^+$ and $Br^-$.
options.C: Incorrect. This shows $HO^-$ attacking the carbon at the same time as Br leaves, which is the single step of an $S_N2$ mechanism. A tertiary halogenoalkane is too hindered for $S_N2$ and reacts by $S_N1$.
options.D: Incorrect. This also wrongly includes $HO^-$ attack in the first step, suggesting $S_N2$. In addition, the curly arrow for the C-Br bond is not drawn correctly onto the Br atom.
